title: One-proportion test
design: One germination outcome per seed under a fixed salt treatment.
data_characteristics: Compare a population probability with a prespecified benchmark
other_examples: Hatching success against a breeding target
Fraction of cells expressing a marker
question: Does the germination probability differ from the 50% benchmark?
options: The reported interval is for one probability
assumptions: Expected successes and failures are sufficiently large.
Seeds sharing an unmodeled tray may be clustered.
parametric: Use a binomial GLM to include dose or genotype.
Use a binomial mixed model to account for trays.
nonparametric: Use binom.test for an exact small-sample test.
A rank test is not a replacement for binary trial data.

plot_args.note: A filled square marks the estimated probability.

code_simulate:
set.seed(3102)
d <- data.frame(seed = 1:120,
                germinated = rbinom(120, 1, 0.67))
write.csv(d, file.path(out_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
par(mar = c(5, 3, 2, 1), las = 1)
plot(estimate, 1, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(.7, 1.3), yaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Germination probability", ylab = "", bty = "n", type = "n")
abline(v = 0.5, lty = 2, col = "#777777")
segments(ci[1], 1, ci[2], 1, lwd = 4, col = "#126887")
points(estimate, 1, pch = 15, cex = 2.2)
text(estimate, 1.12, paste(x, "of", nrow(d), "seeds germinated"))
code_analysis:
x <- sum(d$germinated)
fit <- prop.test(x, nrow(d), p = 0.5,
                 alternative = "two.sided", correct = FALSE)
estimate <- x / nrow(d)
ci <- fit$conf.int
practice: What information is lost if you record only a percentage without the number of seeds tested?
generating_model: Generate 120 independent seeds with Bernoulli germination probability 0.67. Every seed has the same probability. No rounding or tray dependence is simulated.
generating_truth: The true germination probability is 0.67 rather than the null benchmark 0.50; the population difference is +0.17.
teaching_point: A binomial proportion is successes out of a known number of trials; arbitrary continuous percentages are different data.
